question.knowledge_point: Finding a Differential Equation That Relates the Velocity and Displacement of a Particle
question.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin $O$ is $x$ meters, its velocity is $v\,m/s$ and its acceleration is $4{x}^{2}\,{m/s}^{2}.$ Which differential equation describes this motion?
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097535/assets/888a2f1f537f7381379a6f85dc850f29b42193eb53938832be8ede47fbe8264a.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $4{x}^{2}\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=4{x}^{2}.
$$

Using the chain rule for differentiation, we can rewrite this equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=4{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, since $v=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},$ we obtain the differential equation

$$
v\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=4{x}^{2}.
$$

judgment.reasoning: All twelve answers agree with their own captured worked solutions. q-32092: the determinant is 5-k; nonintersecting lines require equal slopes, so k=5 and the determinant is zero. q-73566: det(A)=2, so A is invertible, the lines intersect uniquely, and Ax=0 has the zero solution; only II is true. q-71882: A lies on the circle's boundary, while B and C are interior; I and III are true. q-36432: A is interior, while B and C are boundary points; I and II are true. q-105334: P has squared radius 4, so it is excluded from A but belongs to its boundary; Q has squared radius 8 and is interior. q-105336: P gives 4x²+9y²=72 and belongs to A but not its boundary; Q gives 36 and is a boundary point, not interior. For the motion questions, acceleration satisfies a=v dv/dx=d(v²/2)/dx. q-122313 requires negative acceleration toward the origin. q-107998 has a=4x². q-122339 integrates to v²=x²/16+4 and requires the negative root. q-122337 integrates to v²=2(e^(x-3)+1) and requires the positive root. q-122316 integrates (1+x)² dx=dt and uses x(0)=0. q-122351 first gives v=4(x+1)^(1/4), then integration with x(0)=0 gives x=(3t+1)^(4/3)-1. No grade evidence was supplied; confirmation uses the quoted worked solutions.
